context: The filtering defects a real sweep exposed. 31 unreachable rows and 17 wrong-profession rows reached the user as actionable, and nothing errored. Both classes have a tempting wrong fix: matching the bare word remote catches every qualified-remote US posting, and excluding anything containing sales removes the pre-sales engineering roles the user wants. This tests that a sweep drops the right rows, keeps the discriminating ones, and reports a judgement call visibly enough that the user can overrule it.

checklist.name: Qualified remote dropped
checklist.description: A posting whose location is Remote plus a place the user cannot work in, such as Remote - Texas or Remote - California, is dropped with drop_reason location. These are location requirements, not remote roles

checklist.name: work_mode remote did not rescue a US-only row
checklist.description: A row with work_mode remote and a location of Remote U.S. or Remote - Canada is still dropped. A remote role at a US company and a role requiring you to be in the US are different things, and work_mode does not distinguish them

checklist.name: Subdivision matched against a country exclusion
checklist.description: A US state or Canadian province in the location matched the United States or Canada entry in exclude_locations, even though exclude_locations names only countries

checklist.name: Unqualified remote kept
checklist.description: Remote, Remote - Global, Remote - EMEA and Remote, INT are kept. These are genuinely location-independent, and dropping them is the overcorrection this filter invites

checklist.name: Multi-location posting kept on one reachable location
checklist.description: Doha, Qatar; London, UK and London - Hybrid; New York - Hybrid; San Francisco - Hybrid are kept, because one listed location is London. Testing the whole string as one blob drops both

checklist.name: Off-profession roles dropped
checklist.description: Head of Sales EMEA, PR Director, Strategic Account Director, Customer Success Manager and Manufacturing Engineering Manager are dropped with drop_reason function-excluded

checklist.name: Pre-sales engineering roles kept
checklist.description: Solutions Engineer (Upmarket, Pre-Sales), Pre-sales Engineering Manager and Senior Solutions Engineer (Presales) are kept. This is the discriminating case: a bare sales exclusion removes all three, which is worse than the original bug

checklist.name: Dropped rows retained with a reason
checklist.description: Every dropped row is still in pipeline.csv with its drop_reason, not deleted. A later sweep must not rediscover and re-evaluate it

checklist.name: Profession drops named individually
checklist.description: The run report lists function-excluded rows by company and role rather than only counting them. Unlike a location this encodes a judgement that can be wrong, and the user can only overrule a drop they can see

checklist.name: Empty location did not cause a drop
checklist.description: A posting with no location is kept rather than dropped. A results page often omits it, and a false keep costs a glance while a false drop costs a job

checklist.name: Filtering left to upsert
checklist.description: The sweep harvested locations verbatim and let upsert apply the blockers, rather than filtering during extraction. One place deciding what gets dropped is what makes the run report's counts true

checklist.name: Reported what was dropped and why
checklist.description: Told the user the drop counts by reason, so a filter that is too aggressive is visible rather than silently shrinking the pipeline
